subject: general
question: In a certain code language, 'YOUTH' is written as ‘DUBBQ’ and ‘AGENT’ is written as ‘FMLVC’. How will ‘CURVE’ be written in that language?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The logic followed here is:

For, ‘YOUTH' is written as ‘DUBBQ’,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5e609894657078bbb6324affa36b636d4f1e6e7679b14e779856c4f6c907fa5.png] 

For, 'AGENT’ is written as ‘FMLVC',

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5bf92697b9cb8d080959d0602523af5438866464146a11292c1f931e953dd0bb.png] 

Similarly, for '**CURVE**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a23d4220eddb8da5018f567c2c8c9c29bb14a6d5053e688a0d055a690cb818e6.png] 

So, 'CURVE' will be written as '**HAYDN**'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
